intro.heading: Regain Comfort with Gentle Tooth Extraction in Valencia
paragraphs: Tooth pain doesn’t have to disrupt your life. At Valencia Dentistry, we offer expert tooth extraction in Valencia designed to relieve discomfort, stop infections, and support long-term oral health—all in a calm, welcoming environment. Whether you’re dealing with a severely decayed tooth, impacted wisdom teeth, or overcrowding, Dr. Lavi and our caring team use advanced techniques and sedation options to make the process as smooth and stress-free as possible. From same-day appointments to clear recovery instructions, we’re here to support you every step of the way.

understanding.heading: Types of Tooth Extractions Offered at Valencia Dentistry
understanding.intro: Not all tooth extractions are the same. At Valencia Dentistry, we perform two main types of extractions depending on the condition and location of the tooth:

image.alt: Tooth Extractions: treatment at Valencia Dentistry

items.title: Simple Extractions
items.text: Used when a tooth is fully visible in the mouth and can be removed without surgical intervention. These are typically performed on teeth that are loose or damaged beyond repair.

items.title: Surgical Extractions
items.text: Required for teeth that are impacted, broken at the gumline, or not fully erupted—like many wisdom teeth. Surgical extractions involve making a small incision in the gum and may require sectioning the tooth for easier removal.

items.title: Relief from Persistent Pain
items.text: Say goodbye to the aching, throbbing, or sharp pain caused by infection, decay, or pressure from impacted teeth.

items.title: Elimination of Infection
items.text: Removing a severely decayed or infected tooth helps stop the spread of harmful bacteria to other areas of your mouth or body.

items.title: Protection for Surrounding Teeth
items.text: By removing a compromised tooth, you help prevent damage to neighboring teeth and gum tissue.

items.title: Improved Oral Function
items.text: In cases of overcrowding, extraction can improve bite alignment and make room for future treatments like braces or implants.

items.title: Support for Future Restorations
items.text: A timely extraction sets the stage for long-term solutions like dental implants, bridges, or dentures.

process.heading: Our Tooth Extraction Process: What to Expect
process.intro: At Valencia Dentistry, we make the tooth extraction process as smooth and stress-free as possible. Whether it’s a simple or surgical procedure, Dr. Lavi and our experienced team walk you through every step with compassion, transparency, and personalized care.

steps.title: Consultation & Digital Imaging
steps.text: We begin with a comprehensive exam and 3D imaging to assess the tooth and surrounding structures. Dr. Lavi will discuss your symptoms, explain your options, and determine whether an extraction is the right solution for you.

steps.title: Comfortable Tooth Removal
steps.text: The extraction is performed right in our Valencia office using local anesthesia to fully numb the area. For anxious patients, we also offer sedation options. Whether the procedure is simple or surgical, Dr. Lavi uses advanced techniques to minimize discomfort and ensure safe removal.

steps.title: Guided Recovery & Follow-Up
steps.text: After the extraction, we provide detailed aftercare instructions and schedule a follow-up to check your healing. Most patients recover quickly and experience significant relief within just a few days. If you plan to replace the tooth, we’ll walk you through your next steps for implants or restorations.

candidate.heading: Who Might Need a Tooth Extraction?
candidate.text: Tooth extractions are typically a last resort—but when a tooth poses a risk to your oral health or daily comfort, removal can provide lasting relief and prevent further complications. You may be a good candidate for a tooth extraction if you’re experiencing:
bullets: Severe tooth decay that cannot be repaired with a filling, crown, or root canal
Infection or abscess that has spread to the pulp or surrounding bone
Impacted wisdom teeth causing pain, swelling, or shifting of other teeth
Advanced periodontal disease that has loosened the tooth’s foundation
Overcrowding that interferes with orthodontic treatment or bite alignment
Cracked or fractured teeth beyond restoration due to trauma or grinding

extra.heading: How to Care for Your Mouth Before and After a Tooth Extraction
paragraphs: Proper care before and after your extraction helps ensure a smooth procedure and quick, comfortable healing. At Valencia Dentistry, we provide personalized guidance every step of the way so you can feel confident and cared for.
bullets: Avoid smoking or alcohol for at least 24 hours prior
Let us know about any medications or health conditions
Eat a light meal (unless sedation is planned)
Arrange transportation if you’ll be receiving sedation
Practice good oral hygiene to reduce infection risk
Rest for the first 24 hours and avoid strenuous activity
Don’t use straws, smoke, or spit forcefully, as this can dislodge the blood clot and cause dry socket
Stick to soft, cool foods like yogurt, smoothies, scrambled eggs, or mashed potatoes
Use ice packs and take any prescribed medications to manage swelling and discomfort
Rinse gently with saltwater after the first 24 hours to keep the area clean

faqs.q: Is getting a tooth pulled painful?
faqs.a: Most patients are surprised at how quick and comfortable the procedure is. We use local anesthesia to numb the area completely, and sedation options are available if you’re feeling anxious. You may feel some pressure—but not pain—during the extraction.

faqs.q: How long does it take to recover after a tooth extraction?
faqs.a: Initial healing typically takes 1–3 days for simple extractions, and about a week for surgical ones. Most patients return to normal activities within a few days, following proper aftercare.

faqs.q: What can I eat after a tooth extraction?
faqs.a: Stick to soft, cool foods for the first couple of days—think yogurt, smoothies, applesauce, and scrambled eggs. Avoid straws, crunchy snacks, or anything too hot until the area has started to heal.

faqs.q: Do I need to replace a tooth after it’s extracted?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes—especially if the extracted tooth isn’t a wisdom tooth. Missing teeth can cause neighboring teeth to shift and affect your bite. We can discuss options like dental implants, bridges, or partial dentures during your follow-up.
